standard_prerequisites.name: A unique factorisation domain is normal, and the class group map of a normal integral scheme is injective, both cited from the algebra chapter and the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives normality and injectivity in the first direction.

standard_prerequisites.name: A prime divisor on a scheme whose local rings are unique factorisation domains is an effective Cartier divisor, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Realizes every prime divisor as a divisor of a section, which gives surjectivity of the class group map.

standard_prerequisites.name: An element of the fraction field of a normal Noetherian domain with prescribed orders at height one primes, with order one at a chosen one and order zero elsewhere, lies in the domain, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a principal generator of each height one prime in the second direction.

standard_prerequisites.name: A Noetherian normal domain all of whose height one primes are principal is a unique factorisation domain, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the local rings are unique factorisation domains.

core_obligations: First direction, normality and injectivity: if the local rings are unique factorisation domains then the scheme is normal, so the class group map is injective (proof lines 6920-6923).

First direction, surjectivity: every prime divisor is then an effective Cartier divisor, and the canonical section of the associated invertible sheaf vanishes exactly along it, so the class of the divisor is in the image of the class group map (proof lines 6924-6932).

Second direction, setting up: assume normality and surjectivity, pick a prime divisor, and choose an invertible sheaf with a regular meromorphic section whose divisor differs from the given prime divisor by a principal divisor, so that the given divisor is the divisor of a meromorphic section of that sheaf (proof lines 6934-6939).

Second direction, local computation: at a point, the local ring is a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field the function field of the scheme, every height one prime corresponds to a prime divisor, and invertible sheaves become trivial on the spectrum of the local ring; consequently for each height one prime there is an element of the fraction field with order one there and order zero at all other height one primes, which lies in the local ring by the cited statement, and every element of that prime is a multiple of it, so the prime is principal and the local ring is a unique factorisation domain (proof lines 6940-6953).
proof_roadmap: Show that UFD local rings give normality, injectivity of the class group map and surjectivity via the Cartier property of prime divisors (proof lines 6920-6932).

Conversely, use surjectivity to write each prime divisor as the divisor of a section, then produce a principal generator of every height one prime of each local ring and conclude unique factorisation (proof lines 6934-6953).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a locally Noetherian integral scheme, having unique factorisation domain local rings is equivalent to being normal with surjective Picard to class group map, in which case that map is an isomorphism (statement lines 6907-6918). The counted proof has two real halves: the first direction combines normality with the fact that prime divisors are effective Cartier divisors to get injectivity and surjectivity of the class group map, and the second direction uses a surjectivity hypothesis to realize a given prime divisor as the divisor of a meromorphic section and then, at each local ring, constructs an element of the fraction field with order one at a chosen height one prime and order zero elsewhere, concludes it lies in the local ring, shows every element of that prime is a multiple of it, and applies the criterion that a Noetherian normal domain with principal height one primes is a unique factorisation domain (proof lines 6920-6953). It is H2: both directions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard normality, divisor and unique factorisation criteria.
